Formulation
Brief summary: The patient presents with work-related stress and fatigue, alongside a new dermatitis episode (hands/arms) likely triggered by swimming or weather; dermatitis is being managed with topical treatments and OTC antihistamines. Stress at work may be contributing to fatigue and overall well-being. Limited social information; no acute safety concerns documented in the transcript.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
Principal Problem: Acute stress related to work
- Patient Goal(s): Manage work-related stress; maintain skin symptom control; improve energy
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce perceived stress; support sleep and daytime energy; monitor mood and functioning
- Actions (Patient): Identify stress triggers; practice coping strategies as feasible; adhere to dermatitis treatment plan; rest as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Acknowledge and document plan; consider additional mental health support if symptoms persist; provide follow-up for overall well-being and dermatitis management

Secondary Problem: Dermatitis with pruritus
- Patient Goal(s): Resolve itching; prevent skin deterioration
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce inflammation and itch; maintain skin barrier with emollients; confirm treatment response
- Actions (Patient): Apply prescribed steroid cream and emollients as directed; use OTC antihistamines as needed; note triggers (e.g., swimming, weather) and avoid where possible
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide steroid cream and emollients; reinforce education on skin care; discuss OTC antihistamines; arrange follow-up in 1 week or as symptoms dictate

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Dermatitis management (topical steroids, emollients, OTC antihistamines); potential triggers (swimming, weather); avoidance of ineffective analgesics (paracetamol not helpful for this issue)
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Not recorded
